paragraphs: The 230i has been part of the BMW 2 Series range since the F22/F23 generation launched in 2014. Early F22/F23 cars (up to around 2016) use the N20 — a 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol engine that's also found across the contemporary BMW line-up. From 2016 onwards, the 230i switched to the B48, a more recent four-cylinder petrol unit that's a different family of engine entirely. The current G42 generation (2021–present) continues with the B48, which is now the established engine for this variant. Knowing which one your car has matters — the known wear pattern and rebuild specifics differ — which is why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 230i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol fitted to the 230i (and 228i/220i) from the F22/F23 generation's launch in 2014 until the 2016 engine update. Known for timing chain guide wear on pre-2016 cars — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N20 rebuild.

The B48 replaced the N20 from approximately 2016 onwards, first in the F22/F23 and then carried over into the G42 generation from 2021. It's a more recent design — generally considered more reliable than the N20, with no equivalent widespread timing-chain issue. We service it to the same standard as our other 230i rebuilds.

compatibility.intro: Because the 230i spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N20 part will work on a B48 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N20 or B48) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 230i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
